fields.meta_description: A brand awareness survey that asks for unprompted recall first, catches overclaiming with a decoy brand, and tracks every market over time.
fields.h1: Build a Brand Awareness Survey That Shows Who Knows You
fields.hero_description: Build a brand awareness survey that asks for unprompted recall before any list, and saves every answer in your own database.
fields.features_heading: The Pieces That Keep Recall Numbers Honest
fields.features_subheading: Each one protects the unprompted answer or the line from one round to the next.
fields.feature_1:
Unprompted recall on a screen of its own

Ask people to type every brand they can name in your category into a blank box. No logo or brand name appears on that screen, and the back button stays off once they move on.
fields.feature_2:
A brand lineup with a decoy mixed in

Show your brand among real rivals in random order, plus one plausible brand that does not exist. The share who tick the invented one sets how far to discount every recognition score.
fields.feature_3:
Typed names matched to the right brand

Write aliases for each brand, such as misspellings and short forms, and each typed answer counts toward the brand it means. Anything the aliases miss waits in a queue for a person.
fields.feature_4:
A first-heard question on your channels

Offer the channels you pay for, such as podcasts or billboards, as the answer options. Each answer is stored against the market and the survey round, ready to set beside spend.
fields.feature_5:
Recall by market, round against round

Chart unprompted and prompted recall per city or region next to the previous round. When a market moves more than the margin you set, its owner gets a Slack message or an email.
fields.feature_6:
Responses and source code that stay yours

Keep every response in a database you own, one row per person per round. Export the whole survey app to your GitHub repository on paid plans, then change it with a prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Awareness Studies in the Field
fields.tab_content_1:
Six weeks of billboards, read against a city with none

Juniper Row Cider booked six weeks of billboards in Denver and none in Omaha. Before and after, 400 cider drinkers per city picked the brands they knew. Denver climbed to 152 from 84. Omaha drifted to 88 from 80 without a single billboard, and lift is whatever Denver gained beyond that.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four regions, one made-up insurer in the list

Every quarter, 600 pet owners type every pet insurer they can name into a blank box. Only then do they see a list that hides Hollis Pet Cover, a made-up insurer, among the real ones. Thirty claimed to know it. In the Midwest, 6 of 150 named Fernway unprompted, and the regional manager got that number by email.
fields.tab_content_3:
One question on the order confirmation page

Right after checkout, Oakhollow's order confirmation page asks one thing: "Where did you first hear about us?" The answer is saved on the order. In September a home design podcast led with 384 of 1,200 answers, ahead of search at 276, and topped the Monday post to the marketing channel.
fields.tab_content_4:
The logo without the name, in a new city

Before the first truck rolls in Phoenix, 300 homeowners there see the Copperline Movers logo on their phones, name blurred, and type whose they think it is. Only 27 of the 300 named Copperline. In Tucson, its home city, 132 of 300 did. The first Phoenix mailers print the name in large type beside the logo.

fields.howto_title: How to Design a Brand Awareness Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to design a brand awareness survey that measures recall honestly and tracks it by market, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the category and the market
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for brands with no prompt
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Show the lineup, with one decoy
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the category you compete in the way a buyer would say it, such as pet insurance instead of your product line. Then fix the market: the cities or regions you sell in, plus one screening question that keeps only people who buy in the category.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask people to name every brand they can think of in that category before any name or logo appears. The first brand typed is top-of-mind, and the full answer is unprompted recall. Anything shown earlier would inflate both numbers.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Next, show your brand among the rivals buyers weigh in random order, and add one believable brand that does not exist. Anyone who ticks the decoy is overclaiming, and that share tells you how far to discount recognition.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For people who recognize your brand, ask where they first came across it. Offer the channels you spend on, like podcasts or trade shows, alongside word of mouth, and keep those options identical in every round you run.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Field a full round before a campaign starts, in the markets that will see it and in one that will not. Without the before numbers and a control market, a rise after launch could be the season or a rival's advertising.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Freeze the wording and the sample
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run the next wave with the same wording, the same random ordering, and the same screening question. Changing who qualifies or how the category is named moves the score on its own and breaks the comparison with earlier waves.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Show unprompted and prompted recall for each market beside the previous wave, with the decoy rate next to them. Put the weakest market in front of the person who owns it, and judge the next campaign by whether that number moves.

plan.angle: The top 10 (SurveyMonkey, Qualtrics, Attest, Typeform, Formbricks, Checkbox, Zinklar, LimeSurvey, CloudResearch, NewtonX) are question banks and templates: unaided versus aided wording, a sample list, a download. None shows an awareness study once it runs: a baseline taken before a campaign and a control city to read it against, recall split by region with a made-up brand in the list to catch overclaiming, a where-did-you-hear question tied to each order, and a logo shown without its name in a market the brand is about to enter. This page answers the question-bank intent in the FAQ and how-to, then shows those four studies running. The brand perception sibling owns how people rate a brand they know; this page owns whether they know it at all.
tab_stories: A cider maker surveys 400 cider drinkers in Denver and 400 in Omaha before and after six weeks of Denver billboards, and aided recognition climbs 17 points in Denver against 2 in Omaha.
A pet insurer asks 600 owners each quarter to name insurers unprompted, then shows a list that includes one invented insurer, and the Midwest trails every other region on unprompted recall.
An online furniture store asks every buyer on the order confirmation page where they first heard of the store, and a podcast ad leads September with 384 of 1,200 answers.
Before opening in Phoenix, a moving company shows 300 local homeowners its logo with the name hidden, and only 27 can name the company against 132 of 300 in its home city.

claims_to_source: A brand awareness survey measures whether people know a brand, through unaided recall (naming brands with no prompt) and aided recognition (picking from a list)
Unaided recall must be asked before any brand name appears, because a list shown first inflates the unaided score
Top-of-mind awareness is the share of people who name the brand first in unaided recall
A plausible fictional brand in the aided list catches overclaiming, and its recognition rate shows how much to discount recognition scores
A campaign's effect on awareness is read by comparing people who were exposed with a control group that was not
Tracking waves need identical questions and a fixed sample definition, or the change between waves is artificial

scope.evidence: H1 "Build a Brand Awareness Survey That Shows Who Knows You", meta title "Brand Awareness Survey Template and Questions | Emergent" and hero "Build a brand awareness survey that asks for unprompted recall before any list, and saves every answer in your own database." (under 130 chars) cover the whole job; how-to description is one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 are question banks and templates; the page gives the question order (FAQ 3, how-to 02-04), a template outline (FAQ 6: "the screener, the open recall box, a shuffled set of names with one decoy, and the first-heard question, in that order") and four running studies.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: "top-of-mind", "decoy rate", "control market", "Denver climbed to 152 from 84. Omaha drifted to 88 from 80 without a single billboard".

openers.evidence: Every feature body opens on a verb ("Ask people to type", "Show your brand", "Write aliases", "Offer the channels", "Chart unprompted", "Keep every response"); tabs open on full sentences.

craft.evidence: Short declaratives, one idea each: "No logo or brand name appears on that screen, and the back button stays off once they move on." QC Q2/Q5 clean; craft items are notes only.

voice.evidence: Reads operator-written: "lift is whatever Denver gained beyond that"; "A sample of customers alone overstates awareness, since every one of them knows the brand." Terminology drift (round/wave) is a note.

truth.evidence: Domain facts sourced (unaided first, top-of-mind, decoy brand, control market, fixed waves); claims_used prompt-build, database-owned, code-export, alerts, no-caps all approved; 152-84-(88-80)=60, 384+312+276+228=1,200, 6 of 150, 27/132 of 300 agree across copy, alt and images.

distinct.evidence: Owns whether people know the brand; perception sibling is linked and scoped out in FAQ 3: "How people rate a brand they already know is the job of a brand perception survey". Cross-page formula reuse is a note.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, no brand or file-format asks, hub link in item 2, sibling links in items 3 and 7, each answered first ("Unaided questions give no hints: people name brands from memory.").

images.evidence: Four tabs each show one moment matching the copy: "Denver: 84 to 152 / Omaha: 80 to 88", "Midwest: 6 of 150 / Named Fernway unprompted", "Podcast leads: 384 of 1,200", "Phoenix: 27 of 300 / Tucson: 132 of 300"; one hero each, text readable.

findings.field: feature_4, feature_5, feature_6, faq, howto_step_6_des, howto_step_7_des, mockup, tab_image_2
findings.issue: Two terms for one survey cycle and four for aided recognition. Cycle: "round" in feature_4 ("the survey round"), feature_5 ("the previous round"), feature_6 ("per round"), FAQ 2 ("every round"), FAQ 9 ("each round"), FAQ 10 ("previous round"), versus "wave" in howto_step_6_des ("the next wave", "earlier waves") and howto_step_7_des ("the previous wave"). Aided measure: "prompted recall" (feature_5, howto_step_7_des), "recognition" (feature_2, howto_step_3_des), "Aided questions" (FAQ 4), "listed recall" (mockup, tab_image_2 alt), "From list" (image).
findings.fix: Pick round or wave and one name for the aided measure, and use them everywhere.

findings.issue: Soft quantifiers about no named third party: FAQ 1 "and often where they first heard of each one"; FAQ 4 "usually the smaller number"; FAQ 9 "quarterly fits most brands".
findings.fix: State the condition instead of the frequency word where possible.

findings.issue: The copy names search as the comparison point, which reads as the runner-up, but the image shows Friend or family second at 312 and search third at 276. Not false, but a reader comparing copy and image sees a skipped row.
findings.fix: Name the runner-up: "ahead of friend or family at 312", or say search came third.

findings.issue: The phone screen asks about a logo and says "Name blurred on the logo", but no logo is drawn; the typed answer "Seen it on a truck" also sits oddly with the copy's "Before the first truck rolls in Phoenix".
findings.fix: Draw a blurred logo tile on the phone screen and use a guess such as "Desert Van Lines?" instead of the truck line.

findings.quote: In the Midwest, 6 of 150 named Fernway unprompted
findings.issue: The brand running the survey, Fernway, first appears in the last sentence; until then the reader does not know whose recall is being measured.
findings.fix: Open with the insurer: "Every quarter, Fernway asks 600 pet owners to type...".

findings.quote: Export the whole survey app to your GitHub repository on paid plans, then change it with a prompt.

findings.fix: Coordinator: add a ranking survey tool (e.g. Qualtrics or LimeSurvey) to the library, then rebuild the table.
